title: Board Policy on Capital Credits (Patronage Capital): One Capital Account per Member per Patron Class
content:
# One Capital Account per Member per Patron Class

**Policy.** Under Capital Credits (Patronage Capital), a member holds one capital credit account per patron class, opened at the member's first allocation in that class. A member billed on schedules of two classes — a farm home and an irrigation pivot, for example — holds two accounts. A second account in the same patron class is never opened for the same member; later allocations post to the existing account whatever its status, except that an account in fully retired status is reopened only by a new allocation, which posts to a new account.

**Basis of the record.** Whether a member already holds an account in a class is read from the system record of the member's capital accounts — the member, the patron class and the account's status — as it stands before the allocation is booked. A member's own statement about the accounts held does not replace that record.

## How the rule reads in practice

| The member's existing account in the patron class | Where the next allocation in that class posts |
|---|---|
| none | a new account, opened at this first allocation |
| one account, active | that existing account |
| one account, inactive | that existing account |
| one account, estate claim pending | that existing account |
| one account, fully retired | a new account, opened by the new allocation |

- The limit is one account per class, not one account per member: the number of classes in which a member holds an account follows the number of classes whose schedules the member is billed on, with no other cap.
- Two service accounts on rate schedules of the same class (two Schedule R homes, or a Schedule GS-1 shop and a Schedule GS-3 bin site) feed one capital account in that class.

## Hypothetical cases

1. A member billed on Schedule FH and Schedule IR is allocated in the Farm Patron Class and in the Irrigation Patron Class for the first time in the same June. Two accounts are opened, one in each class.
2. A member whose Residential Patron Class account went inactive after a move is allocated again in that class. The allocation posts to the inactive account; no second Residential Patron Class account is opened.
3. A member's Seasonal Patron Class account is fully retired, and the member is later allocated in that class again. The allocation posts to a new Seasonal Patron Class account.
